name: @the-inclusionist/game-soccer
description: Association football on the accessibility-first Inclusionist engine. Reimplemented from a feature description, not forked from any unlicensed source.
comment:name: Package `@the-inclusionist/game-soccer` in repository `the-inclusionist/game-soccer` (ADR-0082).
They MIRROR each other, so there is nothing to hold in the head. `game-<slug>` and not
`the-inclusionist-game-<slug>`, because ADR-0071 §1 says the organisation already names the
container and repeating it would say the word twice.
comment:private: `private: true` UNTIL there is something to publish. ADR-0068 §3 says a game publishes itself as a
package so the catalogue's manifest can select it, and that day this line comes off. A scaffold that
could be published by accident is worse than one that cannot be published at all.

scripts.validate: npm run typecheck && vitest run && npm run build

comment:dependencies: THE ENGINE COMES FROM THE REGISTRY, and this line is the one ADR-0072 was waiting for. It used to read
`file:../SP-the-inclusionist-tracer`, which is `npm link` with another spelling: a symlink walks
straight past the `files` field, so a packaging defect stays invisible until somebody else installs.
The engine was published on 2026-09-06 and this repository stopped being a special case the same day.

⚠️ AND THE CARET IS BACK, WHICH IS THE RULE THIS FIELD ALREADY WROTE DOWN. It used to be pinned exactly because 8.0.0 was only a release candidate on a tag, and the line said it becomes a caret the day the version is `latest`, with the suite as its proof. Measured 2026-09-11: `latest` is 9.0.0, so it is `^9.0.0`, and `npm run validate` is green on it.
⚠️ AND IT IS ALSO WHY THIS REPOSITORY IS NOW REPRODUCIBLE. Reading the engine folder live meant every
build depended on whatever the other session had saved that minute; a version does not move under you.
`pixi.js` is pinned to the engine's EXACT peer version: two PixiJS in one page is a bug, not a

⚠️ AND THE `@mintplex-labs/piper-tts-web` LINE IS GONE, BECAUSE THE REASON FOR IT WAS FALSE. It said `dist-pkg/platform/tts.js` imports the package at runtime while the engine declares it as a DEV dependency, so the import would not resolve for anyone installing from the registry. ⏱ Measured 2026-09-11 against BOTH the installed 8.0.0 and the published 9.0.0: the string `mintplex` appears in `platform/tts.js` exactly twice, and both are COMMENTS. There is no import, no `require` and no dynamic `import()` anywhere in `dist-pkg`. ADR-0094 put that one line on the GAME's side - the engine owns the voices and the game names the provider - so the engine is right not to declare it.

⚠️ AND NOTHING HERE IMPORTED IT EITHER: zero hits across `app`, `tests` and `scripts`. This game declines the neural voice (`semVozNeural`), so it never passes `carregarVozNeural` and never needed the provider at all. The cost was not theoretical - `piper-tts-web` peers on `onnxruntime-web`, which npm installs, and `node_modules` went from 269 MB to 127 MB when the line came out. `npm run validate` is green without it.

⚠️ AND WHETHER THE CLAIM WAS EVER TRUE IS NOT KNOWN, which is said rather than guessed: it may have been accurate against 7.0.1 and gone stale when ADR-0094 moved the import, or it may have been wrong when written. Either way a claim about somebody else's package needs re-reading every time the dependency moves, which is the rule `docs/ENGINE-AUDIT.md` already states and this line was outside of.
